newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty hits highs at 3.4 pct vs basket, depos lower.
newsitem.headline: Zloty hits highs at 3.4 pct vs basket, depos lower.

text.p: The Polish zloty hit an all time high against the basket of currencies firming to 3.4 percent from the trading band centre on Tuesday on exports inflows and foreign purchases of Polish treasuries, dealers said.
They said the zloty climbed even to 3.5 percent from the parity rate in midday, but was pushed off those highs by the dollar's rise on world markets.

"There might have been large client orders on the market," said Marek Wieczorkowski from Kredyt Bank SA. "Foreigners were likely hunting for three-month and 52-week T-bills and some four-year T-bonds," another dealer said.

The zloty closed at 3.40/3.37 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Monday's 3.24/3.20 percent. It closed at 2.9010/20 to the dollar, up from 2.9040/50 on Monday and at 1.8282/88 to the mark against 1.8287/94.
The central bank did not intervene on the forex market, but was checking the price levels.

One-day rates traded lower on a slightly overliquid market despite the central bank's NBP-bill sale. The NBP sold 142 million zlotys of 91-day NBP-bills at an average yield up 0.01 point at 22.00 percent and 152.6 million zlotys of 182-day NBP-bills at an average yield 0.01 point down at 21.99 percent.
The NBP drained also 394 million zlotys from the market for six days at a maximum rate of 21.63 percent.

Poland's broad money rose by 6.57 billion zlotys, or 5.1 percent in December to 134.49 billion after a 1.4 pct rise in November. Broad money supply grew 29.0 percent in 1996 against 31.5 percent in 1995.
Players said such a big rise of broad money rekindled expectations of a near-term interest rate rise.
"Broad money has risen significantly, so an interest rate rise is quite possible now," said Marek Jezierski from PBI SA.
